---
title: Efficient and Tidy Manipulation of Annotated Matrix Data with plyxp
abstract: >
  In order to manipulate high-dimensional omics data, such as bulk or single cell gene expression counts matrices, a bioinformatics analyst must typically learn domain-specific functions and syntax.

  These matrix-centric functions and syntax may not be as straightforward as working with tidy data analytic principles using tools such as dplyr applied to tabular data.

  We propose an expressive grammar for manipulating annotated matrix data, with syntax to compute on and update matrix data and tabular row and column metadata, including row-wise or column-wise grouped operations.

  This grammar works by defining multiple contexts, and providing pronouns for specific recall and assignment in these contexts.

  The plyxp package is implementation of this grammar for the R/Bioconductor ecosystem, with efficient abstractions for the SummarizedExperiment class. 

  We demonstrate plyxp's efficiency compared to alternative approaches on data manipulation tasks requiring computation across contexts.
